label: defeated opponent
definition: The first competitor won a contest against the second competitor.
scope_notes: Defeat/victory/sweep form the dominant winning family when grouped; lose-to is the strongest individual competing path and has the opposite direction. Mere participation or a margin/lead without an established victory is excluded. Wins and losses in different historical contests may coexist; one explicit win suffices.

facts.reason: The Giants have an explicit victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The separate lose-to row is opposite-direction evidence but need not describe the same event.
The Giants' victory over the Jets directly supplies the declared direction.
The supplied rows say John plays Manhattan and loses to Manhattan; neither establishes a John victory.
A margin over Gore alone is not a completed victory, and the other row explicitly says Bush loses to Gore. No supplied row establishes the declared winning fact.
The Nets explicitly defeat and rout the Knicks. Play and lose rows are mixed event evidence, not grounds to discard the direct win support.
